question: Consider $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ defined by $f(n)=n+3$. Identify one element of the co-domain which has no pre-image and hence determine whether $f$ is onto.
explanation:
Step 1: For $f$ to be onto, every element of the co-domain $\mathbb{N}$ must have at least one pre-image in $\mathbb{N}$.
Step 2: Suppose $1$ has a pre-image $n$. Then $f(n)=1$.
Step 3: Using $f(n)=n+3$, we obtain $n+3=1$, so $n=-2$.
Step 4: But $-2\notin\mathbb{N}$, so there is no natural number mapped to $1$.
Step 5: Therefore, at least one element of the co-domain has no pre-image.
Final Answer: The element $1$ has no pre-image, so $f$ is not onto.

options.A: $4$ has no pre-image; therefore, $f$ is not onto
options.B: $5$ has no pre-image; therefore, $f$ is onto
options.C: $1$ has no pre-image; therefore, $f$ is not onto
options.D: $6$ has no pre-image; therefore, $f$ is onto
